import struct, glob, os, base64, re

block_dir = '/db/.disk_blocks'
# Only numeric block files are part of original file; garbage files contain corrupted/test data
import fnmatch
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(block_dir, 'block_*.bin')))
print(files)
blocks = {}
for f in files:
    base = os.path.basename(f)
    # skip garbage blocks: filename must be block_NNN.bin with digits only
    suffix = base[len('block_'):-len('.bin')]
    if not suffix.isdigit():
        print(f'skip non-numeric {base}')
        continue
    data = open(f,'rb').read()
    assert len(data) == 64, f'{base} unexpected size {len(data)}'
    seq = struct.unpack('<I', data[:4])[0]
    payload = data[4:]  # 60 bytes
    print(f'{base}: seq={seq}')
    blocks[seq] = payload

# Reassemble in sequence order
seqs = sorted(blocks.keys())
print('seqs:', seqs)
# Verify contiguous from 0
assert seqs == list(range(min(seqs), max(seqs)+1)), 'non-contiguous'
recon = b''.join(blocks[s] for s in seqs)
# Remove trailing null padding
recon = recon.rstrip(b'\x00')
print(recon.decode())
print('---')
# Data extraction: [credentials] section
text = recon.decode('utf-8', errors='strict')
# isolate credentials section
m = re.search(r'\[credentials\](.*?)\[(?:backup|\w+)\]', text, re.DOTALL)
cred = m.group(1) if m else text
print(repr(cred))
b64vals = re.findall(r'ENCRYPTED_KEY=([^\s]+)', cred)
print(b64vals)
XOR_KEY = 0x5A
plain_keys = []
for v in b64vals:
    raw = base64.b64decode(v.strip())
    dec = bytes(b ^ XOR_KEY for b in raw).decode('utf-8')
    print(v, '->', dec)
    plain_keys.append(dec)

def is_valid(k):
    if len(k) != 32: return False
    if not k.startswith('AES256'): return False
    if not k.endswith('HASH'): return False
    if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Z0-9]+', k): return False
    if not any(ch.isdigit() for ch in k[6:10]): return False
    if not any(ch.isalpha() for ch in k[-8:-4]): return False
    return True

valid = sorted(k for k in plain_keys if is_valid(k))
print(valid)
with open('/db/recovered_keys.txt','w') as out:
    for k in valid:
        out.write(k + '\n')
print('wrote /db/recovered_keys.txt')
